=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1166-1171 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A routed planning block carries both `ai:blocked` and `ai:scope-blocked`, but the `/answer` transition runs only `--add-label 'ai:planning' --remove-label 'ai:blocked'`. `ai:scope-blocked` stays on the issue, so on a later `/approved` the implement.yml:2544-2548 gate exits with `reason=scope_blocked` (`SKIP_IMPLEMENT=true`).
  WHY: The blocked comment still tells people to reply `/answer`, but an issue a person answers now stops at implement until someone removes `ai:scope-blocked` by hand. A later unblock-judge `override_guard` grant on the stale marker could also post `/approved` against the person's new plan. All reviewers rated it MAJOR. The glm reviewer anchored it at plan.yml:2637-2649 and cited 1166-1171 as the place where the problem shows up.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2646-2656 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: Adding `ai:scope-blocked` to a routed planning block fires the `issues: labeled` trigger in internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml (lines 3-5, allowlist line 21). Each routed block therefore starts a full workflow-failure-heal report: issue, comment, run and user API reads plus a `repository_dispatch`. The intake (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:4267-4278) escalates it as a scope-blocked guard rejection.
  WHY: An ordinary planning scope gap that the unblock judge should handle costs an extra runner job and several API calls on every routed block. This contradicts the §15 "no new GitHub API calls" constraint, §26 runner hygiene and the README/changelog claim that "the only extra call is one `gh label create`". It can also open heal issues for something that is not a pipeline failure. Reviewers agreed: all rated it MAJOR, with confidence 3-4.
- .github/workflows/internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml:21 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The label-event trigger list includes `ai:scope-blocked`, so every routed planning block implicitly dispatches workflow_failure_heal.yml. That workflow makes several API reads (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh:166-173 and others), and the intake treats the event as an automation-path guard rejection. The PR adds no gate on the heal side.
  WHY: Each routed block queues a heal run (a runner slot plus about 3-5 API calls) and posts a heal report, with no documented reason and no kill switch. The README/changelog understate this cost. The reviewer reported it twice, under performance and under implicit execution, and both entries are merged here.
- scripts/plan_scope_block_route.sh:96-141 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The router's fence-stripping regex (FENCE_RE at line 98, applied at 130-141) removes only fully closed fenced blocks. A `SCOPE_MISSING:` line inside an unmatched opening fence stays in the parse file, and the router accepts it. Related lines: plan.yml:2298-2303 and 2365-2370.
  WHY: A planner reply with an unclosed fence that contains example `BLOCKED:`/`SCOPE_MISSING:` lines gets labeled `ai:scope-blocked` and routed to `override_guard`, even though the routing rule says fenced scope lines must be ignored. Severity disagreement: gemini and luna rated it MAJOR at confidence 4, glm rated it NIT at confidence 3. The highest rating is used here.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2647-2659 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `ensure_label_exists "ai:scope-blocked" ... || true` ignores a failure to create the label, and the combined label edit that follows still tries to add it next to `ai:blocked`. That edit's failure is also ignored.
  WHY: GitHub rejects the combined edit when the label is missing. The issue is left in `ai:planning` with neither `ai:blocked` nor `ai:scope-blocked`, yet the blocked comment is still posted, so the issue is not reliably parked for the unblock judge.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "It keeps every existing line of that comment and the `ai:blocked` label, so a person can still answer as before." (linked issue, Approach → Planning scope routing)
  expected_change_site: the `/answer` label transition in .github/workflows/plan.yml (lines 1166-1171), which should also clear `ai:scope-blocked` in the same `gh issue edit`, plus a contract test in tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: neither the PR diff nor the last-run diff touches plan.yml:1166-1171, which still removes only `ai:blocked`; implement.yml:2544-2548 refuses to run implementation while `ai:scope-blocked` is present; no test in tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py or tests/test_unblock_judge.py covers a routed planning block that a person answers; gemini also named scripts/unblock_actions.py as a possible change site
- requirement: "§15: no new GitHub API calls ... The label is created with the existing ensure_label_exists helper only when it is absent; that helper's read already runs for ai:blocked." (linked issue, Constraints)
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/plan.yml, "Handle blocked planning output" (routed-label handling and the `ensure_label_exists` call at line 2648), or the heal trigger path so that a routed planning block causes no heal report
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: plan.yml:2648 adds a separate `ensure_label_exists "ai:scope-blocked"` call that shares no read with the `ai:blocked` ensure at line 2653; scripts/label_helpers.sh:193-206 caches per repository and label and invokes `gh label create`; the label added at plan.yml:2649 triggers internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml:21, whose heal report makes several API calls (workflow_failure_heal_report.sh:110, 125, 140, 172) and dispatches another workflow; the PR adds no guard against this; the README and changelog.d/9534-judge-scope-gaps.md describe the cost only as "one gh label create"; glm explicitly declined to flag this gap because the last run already corrected the docs
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:1166-1171 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `/answer` transition (`--add-label 'ai:planning' --remove-label 'ai:blocked'`) leaves `ai:scope-blocked` on a routed block. The label is touched only at plan.yml:2633, 2648 and 2649. implement.yml:2544-2548 then exits with `reason=scope_blocked`, and the unblock scan still resolves the item to `scope-blocked` (unblock_ledger.BLOCK_LABELS line 143) using the stale marker.
  WHY: An issue a person answers stalls at implement until the label is removed by hand. If the judge later grants `override_guard`, the `planning_scope_block` check (scripts/unblock_actions.py line 1162) is false and the grant posts `/approved` against the person's new plan. Suggested fix: also pass `--remove-label 'ai:scope-blocked'` in plan.yml:1170-1171, and add a test in tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:2646-2656 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Adding `ai:scope-blocked` fires the internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml `issues: labeled` trigger (lines 3-5; allowlist line 21). The reporter (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh lines 99-105, 110, 125, 140, 166-172, 176-186) has no exception for planning blocks. The intake (scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh lines 4267-4278) escalates the event.
  WHY: Every routed planning scope gap becomes a heal escalation, an extra runner job and 4+ API calls. This violates §15 and §26 and contradicts the README/changelog. Suggested fix: skip in workflow_failure_heal_report.sh when LABEL is `ai:scope-blocked` and the issue also has `ai:blocked`.
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "It keeps every existing line of that comment and the `ai:blocked` label, so a person can still answer as before." | Expected change site: /answer transition in .github/workflows/plan.yml (lines 1166-1171) + contract test in tests/test_plan_clarify_blocked_output.py | Evidence of absence: the transition is unchanged and removes only `ai:blocked`; implement.yml:2544-2548 refuses to run; no test covers it | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- TASK_GAP: Requirement: "§15: no new GitHub API calls ... ensure_label_exists helper only when it is absent; that helper's read already runs for ai:blocked." | Expected change site: .github/workflows/plan.yml "Handle blocked planning output", or the heal trigger path | Evidence of absence: the label added at plan.yml:2649 triggers internal-workflow-failure-heal.yml:21; the heal report makes calls at workflow_failure_heal_report.sh:110, 125, 140, 172; there is no guard, and the README/changelog/plan.yml comment describe only `gh label create` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
- HARDENING (risk score 3): plan.yml lines 1170-1171 should add `--remove-label 'ai:scope-blocked'` (about 4 lines). scripts/workflow_failure_heal_report.sh around lines 114-122 should log `skip reason=planning_scope_block` and exit 0 when the labels include `ai:blocked` (about 4 lines). (2 related items)
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: An unclosed fence leaves its `SCOPE_MISSING:` lines in the input, so the router may wrongly mark non-scope-blocked issues `ai:scope-blocked`.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:around lines 1166-1171 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4

  WHY: implement.yml line 2544 sees the label and refuses to run implementation, so the person's answer has no effect.

  WHY: This adds an extra runner job and unneeded API calls on every routed block, which violates §15 "no new GitHub API calls".
